title: Anthropic API Pricing 2026: Cost Per Million Tokens
summary: Anthropic API pricing has separate rates for input and output tokens, varying by Claude model. Review the per-million-token costs to budget your API usage.
body_markdown:
## Why output tokens and long prompts increase costs


**Your bill follows how much the model writes and how much you send, not the headline rate, because output tokens cost five times input on every current Claude model.** That's the per-token arithmetic, and it rewards doing the sum per request.


### The input-to-output price ratio


Per[Anthropic's pricing page](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/about-claude/pricing) :


- Haiku 5.5 costs $0.10 in and $0.50 out per million tokens, making output the primary cost lever
- Sonnet 5.5 is[$2](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/models/haiku-5-5/overview) and $10
- Opus 5.5 is[$4](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-opus-5-5) and $20
- Fable 5.1 is[$10](https://www.anthropic.com/claude-fable-and-mythos-5-1) and $50


Because the ratio never changes, a model that writes a lot costs five times more per token than one that mostly reads.


At $2 in and $10 out per million tokens, the chart prices two Sonnet workloads, so output fees dominate the pricing structure.


> Because the ratio never changes, a model that writes a lot costs five times more per token than one that mostly reads.


Chat (500 in, 800 out) costs $9.00 per 1,000 requests, and extraction (4,000 in, 200 out) costs $10.00, meaning low output tokens offset extraction's higher input volume.


At Sonnet 5.5's listed $2 and $10, chat costs $9.00 and extraction $10.00.


Eight times the input, and still only about 11% more cost. That is the extraction job against the chat job, because chat spends $12 of its $13.50 on output, while extraction spends $12 of its $15 on input.


Estimate output length before you estimate anything else.


### Extended thinking billed as output


When a request reasons for several thousand tokens before a 200-token answer, it's priced as if it wrote all of them, because thinking tokens are billed at the output rate.


On Opus 5.5 at $20 per million, that reasoning is the largest line on the invoice. Your visible answer is the smallest, so your bill centers on unseen computations rather than final output.


Cap the thinking budget per request, and enable it only on tasks where a cheaper model without it fails your test.


### Long prompt costs in Claude API pricing


Because you resend the same context on every call, long prompts cost more than their token count suggests. A 4,000-token system prompt on Fable 5.1 adds $0.04 per request at $10 per million input tokens.


Across 1,000 requests, that's $40 for text that never changes. Check the pricing page for any premium on prompts above a given length before you design around a large window.


Some tokens you didn't write still land on your bill: tool definitions go into the input, and each tool result you return is billed as input on the next turn.


An agent that makes five tool calls pays for its growing context five times. Count those turns in your per-request estimate, and the cheapest model that passes your task gets cheaper still.
